$comment: Normative cross-implementation conformance vectors for the fleet-bus v1 envelope. See conformance/README.md for the contract a runner must satisfy. Additive-only: appending vectors is a minor change, altering or deleting one is a breaking change and requires a SPEC.md revision.

vectors.name: accept/minimal
vectors.why: The smallest envelope that satisfies every required field.

vectors.name: accept/null-payload
vectors.why: `payload` is required to be PRESENT, not truthy. JSON null is a legal payload.

vectors.name: accept/scalar-payload
vectors.why: `payload` is arbitrary JSON, not necessarily an object.

vectors.name: accept/unknown-field-ignored
vectors.why: SPEC clause 1: v1 is additive-only and consumers MUST ignore unknown fields rather than reject.

vectors.name: accept/unknown-kind
vectors.why: Schema: unknown kinds are logged, not rejected. Only an empty or non-string kind is invalid.

vectors.name: accept/to-null-is-broadcast
vectors.why: Null or absent `to` means broadcast; the subject determines the audience.

vectors.name: accept/from-normalized-case
vectors.why: `from` is NFKC-lowercased before the allowlist check; the accepted envelope carries the canonical form.

vectors.name: accept/from-normalized-fullwidth
vectors.why: NFKC folds fullwidth Latin to ASCII, so a fullwidth claim is the same identity — not a separate one that slips the allowlist.

vectors.name: accept/ts-offset-positive
vectors.why: RFC 3339 numeric offsets are valid, not only the Z form.

vectors.name: accept/ts-fractional-seconds
vectors.why: Sub-second precision is common in generated timestamps and must not be rejected.

vectors.name: accept/baton-complete
vectors.why: A full, self-consistent baton frame at hop zero.

vectors.name: accept/baton-hops-at-warn-threshold
vectors.why: Hop 8 triggers a warning to `origin`; it is explicitly NOT a rejection. Guards against a warn threshold being implemented as a ceiling.

vectors.name: accept/baton-hops-just-under-ceiling
vectors.why: The ceiling is at 16 and is exclusive-below: 15 is the last legal value. Guards an off-by-one in the wrong direction.

vectors.name: accept/no-baton-fields
vectors.why: Baton fields are a v1.x additive extension. Their absence is legal and must not synthesize defaults during validation.

vectors.name: accept/at-size-limit
vectors.why: The size check is `>` max_bytes, not `>=`. An envelope encoding to exactly max_bytes is legal. Generated so the boundary is real rather than approximated.

vectors.name: reject/not-an-object
vectors.why: A JSON array is not an envelope. Guards implementations whose object test is a bare typeof/isinstance that arrays satisfy.

vectors.name: reject/null-envelope
vectors.why: JSON null passes a naive `typeof === 'object'` test.

vectors.name: reject/string-envelope
vectors.why: A bare JSON string decodes successfully and must still be refused.

vectors.name: reject/version-2
vectors.why: A future major version must be refused with its own reason, not silently parsed as v1.

vectors.name: reject/version-string-one
vectors.why: `"1"` is not 1. Guards a loose-equality version check.

vectors.name: reject/version-missing
vectors.why: Absent is not 1.

vectors.name: reject/id-empty
vectors.why: An empty id defeats dedup and audit correlation, so it is refused rather than tolerated.

vectors.name: reject/id-non-string
vectors.why: A numeric id would compare unequal to its string form in the dedup ledger.

vectors.name: reject/kind-empty
vectors.why: Kind selects the payload semantics; empty means the receiver cannot know what it holds.

vectors.name: reject/ts-not-a-date
vectors.why: An unparseable timestamp is refused by both implementations and anchors the reason name.

vectors.name: reject/ts-non-string
vectors.why: An epoch integer is a plausible sender mistake and must not be coerced.

vectors.name: reject/payload-absent
vectors.why: Presence, not truthiness: this vector differs from accept/null-payload by the KEY, not the value.

vectors.name: reject/to-non-string
vectors.why: `to` is a bot name or null; a number would silently fail every recipient comparison instead of erroring.

vectors.name: reject/in-reply-to-non-string
vectors.why: Same class as `to`: a non-string correlation key never matches and never errors.

vectors.name: reject/in-reply-to-null
vectors.why: Null is NOT the absent form for `in_reply_to` — unlike `to`, no null case is defined. Guards implementations that copy the `to` handling.

vectors.name: reject/from-not-in-allowlist
vectors.why: A well-formed name that is not a fleet member. The core trust check.

vectors.name: reject/from-reserved-broadcast
vectors.why: `broadcast` is reserved and must never resolve to an identity EVEN WHEN an operator has listed it in the manifest. That is the whole claim, so this vector carries an allowlist that contains it — with the suite-level allowlist the vector is refused by ordinary membership and stays green after the reserved-name check is deleted.
vectors.mutation_witness: Delete the RESERVED_BOT_NAMES check from normalizeBotName / normalize_bot_name; this vector MUST fail and no other vector may.

vectors.name: reject/from-illegal-characters
vectors.why: A dotted name is subject-shaped, not identity-shaped, and would widen the allowlist match surface.

vectors.name: reject/from-with-whitespace
vectors.why: Leading whitespace survives lowercasing and would defeat a naive membership check that trims nothing.

vectors.name: reject/from-absent
vectors.why: Absent `from` must reach the same refusal as a rejected claim, not throw.

vectors.name: reject/root-id-empty
vectors.why: An empty chain identity collapses every baton chain into one.

vectors.name: reject/root-id-non-string
vectors.why: Same class as `id`: a non-string chain key never matches its own descendants.

vectors.name: reject/origin-not-in-allowlist
vectors.why: Completion frames are addressed to `origin`. An unlisted origin turns the baton into an arbitrary-destination primitive.

vectors.name: reject/origin-not-canonical
vectors.why: Baton names must arrive ALREADY canonical — unlike `from`, they are not normalized on the way in. `DEET` would NFKC-fold to an allowlisted name, so an implementation that normalizes first would wrongly accept it.

vectors.name: reject/owner-not-in-allowlist
vectors.why: `owner` is the current holder; an unlisted holder means no fleet member is accountable for the chain.

vectors.name: reject/owner-non-string
vectors.why: Guards a normalization path that returns null for non-strings and then compares null to the claim.

vectors.name: reject/hops-negative
vectors.why: A negative counter is the reset attack: it buys unlimited further hops under any ceiling check.

vectors.name: reject/hops-string-zero
vectors.why: `"0"` is the practical reset: it is falsy-adjacent, compares as a valid low value under loose typing, and is what a model-written handler emits. Both implementations require a true integer.

vectors.name: reject/hops-float
vectors.why: 8.5 is not an integer. In Python `isinstance(True, int)` and float checks are easy to get wrong; in TS every number is a double.

vectors.name: reject/hops-boolean
vectors.why: Python's bool IS an int subclass, so `type(x) is not int` is load-bearing here and a switch to isinstance would silently admit `true` as hop 1.

vectors.name: reject/oversize
vectors.why: One byte past max_bytes. Generated rather than literal so the boundary is exact.

vectors.name: divergence/hops-at-ceiling
vectors.why: SPEC says reject at 16, and the ceiling must fire on INBOUND wire validation — otherwise a peer publishing `hops: 100` slips past validate and is caught only if the local bot happens to derive a further increment. TypeScript enforces this; Python enforces it only in derive_baton_fields, so it accepts an at-or-over-ceiling frame off the wire.
vectors.resolution: Port the inbound ceiling check into bus.py::validate_envelope. Tracked as INF-036.

vectors.name: divergence/hops-far-over-ceiling
vectors.why: The same gap at a value no legitimate chain can reach, so the fix cannot be mistaken for an off-by-one.

vectors.name: divergence/ts-naive-no-offset
vectors.why: The schema declares `format: date-time`, which is RFC 3339 and requires an offset. A naive timestamp is not a point in time — two bots reading the same audit log disagree about ordering by up to a day. Python requires a trailing Z or numeric offset; TypeScript uses Date.parse, which accepts the naive form and silently interprets it in the host's local zone.
vectors.resolution: Replace Date.parse with an RFC 3339 check in fleet-bus.ts. Held out of the vectors PR because it can drop live frames from any publisher not using toISOString, so it ships on its own. Tracked as INF-037.

vectors.name: divergence/ts-rfc2822
vectors.why: Date.parse also accepts the RFC 2822 form, which no fleet publisher emits and which the schema does not permit. Same root cause as divergence/ts-naive-no-offset, kept separate so a partial fix cannot claim the whole divergence.

vectors.name: reject/ts-offset-minutes-60
vectors.why: Python's fromisoformat NORMALISES `+01:60` to `+02:00` rather than raising, so bus.py carries an explicit regex clamp on the offset fields; Date.parse returns NaN for the same input. Both refuse today and this vector keeps either mechanism from being deleted as redundant — the two reach the same answer by unrelated routes.
